questions.question: For a data set the value of median and mean are respectively 6 and 7, then find the value of mode.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct **empirical relationship** between mean, median, and mode:

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

Mode = 3 × 6 − 2 × 7 = 18 − 14 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Median** = 6

⇒ **Mean** = 7

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/918e2e1b68cdb77d959da3c7adc7956f4533c642b95451a10e6bd6b22672b961.png] 

**Calculations:**

Substitute the given values of **mean** and **median** into the formula:

⇒ Mode = 3 × 6 − 2 × 7

⇒ Mode = 18 − 14

⇒ Mode = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Karl Pearson's Empirical Formula

For moderately asymmetrical distributions, the distance between the mean and the mode is approximately three times the distance between the mean and the median: (Mean − Mode) = 3 × (Mean − Median).

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the values of mean, median, and mode are identical: Mean = Median = Mode.

Positively Skewed Distribution

In a distribution skewed to the right, the values follow the order: Mean > Median > Mode.

Negatively Skewed Distribution

In a distribution skewed to the left, the values follow the order: Mean < Median < Mode.</p

questions.question: If ΔABC and ΔPQR are similar. AB = 8 cm, PQ = 12 cm, QR = 18 cm and RP = 24 cm, then the perimeter of ΔABC is _________ cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Perimeter of ΔPQR = PQ + QR + RP = 12 + 18 + 24 = 54 cm

Ratio of corresponding sides = AB / PQ = 8 / 12 = 2 / 3

Perimeter of ΔABC = 54 × (2 / 3) = 36 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AB = 8 cm

PQ = 12 cm

QR = 18 cm

RP = 24 cm

ΔABC ~ ΔPQR

**Formula Used:**

For two similar triangles, the ratio of their perimeters is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides:

Perimeter(ΔABC) / Perimeter(ΔPQR) = AB / PQ = BC / QR = CA / RP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c915b7e6c39814636414cedc3eaca66decb41a196ad73642c855739f7673ffdb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter of ΔPQR = PQ + QR + RP

⇒ Perimeter of ΔPQR = 12 + 18 + 24 = 54 cm

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / Perimeter(ΔPQR) = AB / PQ

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / 54 = 8 / 12

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / 54 = 2 / 3

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) = 54 × (2 / 3)

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) = 18 × 2 = 36 cm

**Option Analysis:**

**Option (1) 36:** This is the correct perimeter of ΔABC as calculated above.

**Option (2) 54:** This is the perimeter of ΔPQR, not ΔABC.

**Option (3) 27:** This value is incorrect because the ratio of perimeters must be 2:3, which gives 36 cm, not 27 cm.

**Option (4) 42:** This value is incorrect because it does not satisfy the similarity ratio of 2:3 with the perimeter of ΔPQR (54 cm).

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of their perimeters, altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors.

Area Ratio Theorem

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔPQR) = (AB / PQ)².

Criteria for Similarity

Two triangles are similar if they satisfy any of the following criteria: Angle-Angle (AA), Side-Angle-Side (SAS), or Side-Side-Side (SSS).</p

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, PQ, and QR are two chords such that ∠PQR = 118°. What is the measure of ∠OPR?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any triangle **OPR** inscribed in a **circle** with center **O** and chords **PQ** and **QR** forming an angle θ:

Measure of ∠OPR = |∠PQR − 90°|

⇒ ∠OPR = |118° − 90°|

⇒ ∠OPR = 28°

**∴ The correct answer is 28°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠PQR = 118° in a **circle** with **centre O**.

**Formula Used:** Angle at the **center** is twice the angle at the **circumference**. In a **cyclic quadrilateral**, opposite angles sum to 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10bc9a951e070fa64f9c430b5d662c1140734fe4bbe97ca75713591b4e373f58.png] 

⇒ Let **S** be a point on the **major arc PR**. Then **PQRS** is a **cyclic quadrilateral**.

⇒ ∠PSR + ∠PQR = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR + 118° = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR = 62°

⇒ Central **angle** subtended by **arc PR** is ∠POR = 2 × ∠PSR

⇒ ∠POR = 2 × 62° = 124°

⇒ In **▵OPR**, **OP = OR** (**radii** of the same circle).

⇒ ▵OPR is an **isosceles triangle**, so ∠OPR = ∠ORP.

⇒ ∠OPR + ∠ORP + ∠POR = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OPR + 124° = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OPR = 56°

⇒ ∠OPR = 28°

**∴ The correct answer is 28°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle at Center Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circumference.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180° (∠A + ∠C = 180°).

Isosceles Triangle in Circles

Any triangle formed by two radii and a chord is an isosceles triangle because radii of the same circle are equal in length.</p

questions.question: Name the filtration units of the excretory system in human.
questions.solution:
__**Concept**__:

**Human Excretory system:**

__
 
• The system of the organ which is used to remove the waste product out from the body is called** the human excretory system**.
 
• The major waste product generated in the human body is urea, along with which some other toxins are also generated.
 
• Urea is eliminated by kidneys by the process of urination and solid wastes are removed from the body by the intestines.

**Excretory system organs:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e41f1740cdb8115a19d9bbfcf5e898af70219f2d79922d8483412abbbc330bb3.png] 

 
• **Kidneys:**It is a bean shaped organ. Its function is to clean blood and eliminate the waste from the blood in form of urine

 
• It is present in the abdomen, just below the diaphragm, and is protected by ribs.
 
• Each kidney weighs 120g to 170 g and 10-12 cm long and 5-7 cm wide and is the size of a fist.
 
• Kidneys are made up of subunits called Nephron

** **2.**Ureters: **​Each kidney is connected to the rinal pelvis by a thin muscular tube, this tube is called as **Ureter.**

 
• Its function is to propel urine from the kidney to the urinary Bladder from time to time.

 3**.Bladders:** It's the organ that controls the passage of urine, it is a muscular sac-like structure.

 
• The average capacity of the bladder is **400-600 ml.**
 
• It holds urine until its capacity expels, or till it gets full.

 4.**Urethra: **The Urethra is a tube made up of fibro muscular tissue that arises from the lower opening of the bladder, and open to the external uretral orifice.

 
• It helps to expel urine through the body, in the male it is also the tube that consist of the sperms.

**Explanation**__:

__
 
• In kidneys, the Nephron is the functional unit, each kidney has as many as 1 million nephrons in each human kidney.
 
• The basic functions of the **nephron** are to carry **out secretion** as well as the **process of excretion **and also called as** filtration unit of the human excretory system**.
 
• Each nephron is made up of a **Malpighian body.**
 
• **Nephrons** are of two types which are **Cortical Nephrons** and **Juxtamedullary Nephrons**.

**So, the Nephron is the part that is also called as filtration unit of the Excretory unit.__**

questions.question: A circular grass field of diameter 42 m is surrounded by a path of width 3.5 m. What will be the cost of graveling the path at the rate ₹ 4 square meter?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Inner radius (r) = 21 m, Outer radius (R) = 21 + 3.5 = 24.5 m.

**Path Area** = π × (R + r) × (R − r) = (22/7) × 45.5 × 3.5.

**Area** = 11 × 45.5 = 500.5 m².

**Total Cost** = Area × Rate = 500.5 × 4 = ₹ 2002.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 2002.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Inner **diameter** of field = 42 m

**Width** of the path = 3.5 m

**Rate** of graveling = ₹ 4 per m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of **circular path** = π(R² − r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c27bd229553e5e0e99154ac1b9b166454b522df311e8d048f2a53f4deb5a0a83.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Inner radius (r) = 42 ÷ 2 = 21 m

⇒ Outer radius (R) = Inner radius + Width = 21 + 3.5 = 24.5 m

⇒ Area of the path = (22/7) × (24.5² − 21²)

⇒ Area = (22/7) × (24.5 + 21) × (24.5 − 21)

⇒ Area = (22/7) × 45.5 × 3.5

⇒ Area = 11 × 45.5 = 500.5 m²

⇒ **Cost of graveling** = Area × Rate = 500.5 × 4

⇒ Cost = ₹ 2002

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 2002.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of a Circle

The area of a circle with radius r is given by A = πr², where π ≈ 22/7 or 3.14.

Area of a Ring (Circular Path)

The area between two concentric circles is π(R² − r²), which can be simplified using the identity (a² − b²) = (a − b)(a + b).

Cost Calculation

Total cost for any surface work is calculated as: Total Cost = Area × Rate per unit area.

questions.question: When 1542, 1754 and 2125 are divided by the greatest number x , the remainder in each case is y. What is the value of (x - 5y)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers are 1542, 1754, and 2125.

**Concept used:**

HCF is the highest common factor 

If 3 numbers A, B, and C are divided by the greatest number 'x' and leave the same remainder each time, then

The value of x will be HCF of (A - B) (B - C) and (A - C).

**Calculation:**

We have to find HCF of (1754 - 1542), (2125 - 1754), and (2125 - 1542).

⇒ 1754 - 1542 = 212 = 53 × 22

⇒ 2125 - 1754 = 371 = 53 × 7

⇒ 2125 - 1542 = 583 = 53 × 11

HCF of 212, 371, and 583 is 53.

The remainder when 1542 is divided by 53 is 5.

So, x = 53 and y = 5

⇒ x - 5y = 53 - 5 × 5

⇒ 53 - 25 = 28

**∴ The value of (x - 5y) is 28.**

questions.question: Which of the following is distributive property of addition ?
questions.solution:
On checking options - 

Option 1) False, it is commutative property of addition.

Option 2) False, it is the associative property of addition.

Option 3) True, it is the distributive property of addition.

Option 4) False, it is the commutative property of multiplication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Multiplication:

 
• Commutative Property: a × b = b × a. Example, 9 × 4 = 4 × 9 = 36
 
• Associative property: (p × q) × r = p × (q × r) (where p, q, and r are any three natural/whole numbers)
 
• Identity of multiplication: The number ‘1’ has the following special property in respect of multiplication. p × 1= 1 × p = p (where p is a natural number)
 
• Distributive property of multiplication over addition: p × (q + r) = (p × q) + (p × r).

Note that there is no distributive property for addition. One should not be confused (p + q) + r = p + (q + r) as distributive, the given property is associative property for addition.

Addition: When two collections of similar objects are put together, the total of them is called addition.

Properties of addition in natural and whole numbers:

 
• Closure property: Sum of two natural/whole numbers is also a natural/ whole number.
 
• Commutative Property: p + q = q + p where p and q are any two natural/ whole numbers.
 
• Associative property: (p + q) + r = p + (q + r) = p + q + r . This property provides the process for adding 3 (or more) natural/whole numbers.
 
• Additive Identity in Whole Numbers: In the set of whole numbers, 4 + 0 = 0 + 4 = 4. Similarly, p + 0 = 0 + p = p (where p is any whole number). Hence, 0 is called the additive identity of the whole numbers.

• The primary focus of India’s five-year plans has been on achieving self-reliance, economic growth, poverty eradication, and full employment rather than relying on foreign aid.

questions.question: The caloric theory replaced which older theory of heat and combustion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phlogiston theory**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phlogiston theory** was a scientific theory proposed in the late 17th century to explain processes of **combustion and rusting**.
 
• It suggested that a substance called **phlogiston** was released when materials burned or oxidized.
 
• According to the theory, substances rich in phlogiston burned more easily, while substances that had lost phlogiston were considered "dephlogisticated."
 
• The theory was eventually replaced by the **caloric theory** and later by modern theories based on the **laws of thermodynamics** and **atomic structure.**
 
• The work of scientists such as **Antoine Lavoisier** demonstrated that combustion involved the chemical combination of substances with **oxygen**, debunking the phlogiston theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic theory**__

 __
 
• The **Kinetic theory** of heat explains that heat is a form of energy associated with the **random motion of particles** (atoms or molecules) within a substance.
 
• It is a modern theory and is based on **statistical mechanics**, not related to the caloric or phlogiston theories.
 
 
 
• **Thermodynamic theory**__
 __
 
• The **Thermodynamic theory** deals with the principles of energy conservation, heat transfer, and the relationships among temperature, pressure, and volume.
 
• It is a **macroscopic theory** that replaced earlier theories like the caloric theory.
 
 
 
• **Entropy theory**__
 
 
• The **Entropy theory** is part of thermodynamics, describing the degree of **disorder or randomness** in a system.
 
• It has no direct connection with the outdated concepts of caloric or phlogiston theories.

questions.question: Which type of wave is primarily formed on a stretched string when plucked or disturbed?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Transverse wave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transverse waves** are the type of waves that are formed on a **stretched string** when it is plucked or disturbed.
 
• In a transverse wave, the **particles of the medium** move in a direction that is **perpendicular** to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• When a string is plucked, the **up-and-down motion** of the string creates a wave pattern where the crests and troughs are visible.
 
• The wave travels along the length of the string, but the **displacement** of the string particles is at right angles to this direction.
 
• This type of wave is characterized by **wavelength, frequency, amplitude,** and speed.
 
• Examples of transverse waves include **light waves, water waves**, and waves on a string.
 
• Such waves do not require a medium for propagation (if electromagnetic), but on a string, they propagate through the medium of the string material.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Torsional wave**__

 __
 
• **Torsional waves** involve the twisting motion of particles around the axis of wave propagation.
 
• Such waves are commonly found in **solid bars** and structures like **shafts** in mechanical systems.
 
• They are not typically formed on a stretched string.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic wave**__
 __
 
• **Electromagnetic waves** are waves that do not require a medium for propagation and consist of oscillating **electric and magnetic fields.**
 
• Examples include **light, radio waves, and X-rays.**
 
• These waves are not formed on a stretched string as they are inherently different in nature.
 
 
 
• **Surface wave**__
 
 
• **Surface waves** occur at the boundary between two different mediums, such as air and water.
 
• Examples include **water waves**, where the motion of particles is a combination of longitudinal and transverse motion.
 
• These waves are not relevant to the case of a stretched string.

__
 
• **NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar)** is an Earth observation satellite jointly developed by NASA and ISRO.
 
• The satellite is designed to monitor Earth's ecosystem, measure biomass, and study environmental changes.
 
• The commissioning phase of NISAR begins **1 year post-launch**, allowing adequate time for calibration and testing of onboard systems.
 
• During the commissioning phase, the satellite undergoes rigorous validation processes to ensure it meets performance metrics.
 
• The satellite's primary mission includes measuring changes in Earth's surface and providing data on natural disasters like earthquakes, floods, and landslides.

• Although many satellites undergo preliminary testing within 90 days, NISAR's commissioning phase is scheduled after a longer duration to ensure all systems are finely tuned.
 
• In this phase, initial data from the satellite is used for calibration but is not fully operational for scientific purposes.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: After 6 months**

• Its sophisticated dual-frequency radar (L-band and S-band) necessitates more time for testing and validation.

• The satellite's collaboration between NASA and ISRO represents a significant milestone in international space cooperation.

questions.question: Which meristematic tissue is found at nodes and helps in regrowth of grasses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intercalary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Intercalary meristem is a type of meristematic tissue located at the nodes of plants.
 
• It is responsible for the regrowth of grasses and contributes to the elongation of internodes.
 
• Intercalary meristems allow rapid regeneration in grasses after grazing or mowing.
 
• This tissue is present in monocots, particularly in grasses, which aids their survival in environments with regular disturbances.
 
• Unlike apical meristem, which is found at the tips of roots and shoots, intercalary meristem is strategically located at the base of nodes and leaf blades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meristematic Tissue:**

 
 
• Meristematic tissues are responsible for the growth of plants and consist of actively dividing cells.
 
• These tissues are classified into apical, lateral, and intercalary based on their location.
 
• Apical meristem contributes to the primary growth at the tips of roots and shoots.
 
• Lateral meristem is involved in secondary growth, leading to an increase in the girth of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Monocots vs. Dicots:**
 
 
• Monocots, like grasses, have intercalary meristems that help them regrow quickly after damage.
 
• Dicots generally lack intercalary meristems and rely on apical and lateral meristems for growth.
 
 
 
• **Node and Internode:**
 
 
• Nodes are points on the stem where leaves or branches originate.
 
• Internodes are the regions between two nodes, which elongate due to intercalary meristem activity.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation in Grasses:**
 
 
• Grasses are adapted to survive grazing, fire, or mowing due to the presence of intercalary meristems.
 
• These tissues regenerate leaf blades and stems quickly, ensuring survival and growth.

questions.question: Floor of a room measures 4.5 metres × 3 metres. Find the minimum number of complete square marble slabs of equal size required to cover the entire floor.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the minimum number of square slabs, we need the maximum possible size for each slab.

Side of the largest square slab = HCF(4.5 m, 3 m) = 1.5 m

Number of slabs = (Length ÷ Side) × (Breadth ÷ Side)

⇒ Total slabs = (4.5 ÷ 1.5) × (3 ÷ 1.5) = 3 × 2 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 slabs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the floor (L) = 4.5 m = 450 cm

Breadth of the floor (B) = 3 m = 300 cm

**Concept Used:**

To find the minimum number of square slabs, the area of each square slab must be at its maximum.

The maximum side of a square slab that can perfectly fit the dimensions is the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the floor's length and breadth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7001839f2d721a977d84f176561c48050a538fad29bc250075e6c13eb9f0d64.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Side of the maximum square slab = HCF(450 cm, 300 cm)

⇒ HCF of 450 and 300 = 150 cm = 1.5 m

⇒ Area of the floor = Length × Breadth = 4.5 m × 3 m = 13.5 m²

⇒ Area of one square slab = Side × Side = 1.5 m × 1.5 m = 2.25 m²

⇒ Minimum number of slabs required = Area of the floor ÷ Area of one square slab

⇒ Number of slabs = 13.5 ÷ 2.25 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 slabs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Minimum Tiles Required

To minimise the number of tiles needed to cover a rectangular area, the tiles used must be as large as possible. The maximum possible side length of a square tile is mathematically equal to the HCF of the length and breadth of the floor.

Number of Tiles Formula

Total number of tiles = (Area of Floor) ÷ (Area of one Tile). Alternatively, it is the product of the number of tiles fitted along the length and the breadth independently.

Greatest Possible Length

When asked to find the greatest possible length that can be used to measure exactly two or more given lengths, always find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of those dimensions.

questions.question: The ladder is placed against the wall with its upper end touching the wall. The ladder bottom rests on the ground and is 10ft away from the wall and also makes an angle 60° with the ground. After some time, ladder begins to slip and the angle of contact changes to 30° in a minute. Find the rate of slip in ft/sec?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Rate of slip = Total distance for which slip happened ÷ Time taken to slip

cosθ = bover h, where "b" and "h" are the base and height of the right-angled triangle.

**Concept: **

The rate of slip could be considered analogous to speed. It could be found by dividing the total distance travelled by the foot of the ladder in the specified time.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0112612134c580339a92b25c19f23aa4ed8300cdb932c3125d572117a506470.png] 

In Δ AOD,

⇒ cos 60° = ODover AD

⇒ 1over2 = ODover AD

∴ AD = 2 × OD = 20 ft

Let the distance of slip i.e., CD = y ft.

∴ OC = 10 + y

Since AD and CB are the same ladder, AD = CB = 20 ft

In Δ BOC,

⇒ cos 30° = OCover CB

⇒ sqrt3over 2 = OCover 20

∴ OC = 10√3 ft = 10 × 1.73 = 17.3 ft

Equating both values of OC, we get-

⇒ 17.3 = 10 + y

∴ y = 17.3 - 10 = 7.3 ft

Rate of slip = 7.3/60 = 0.12 ft/s

**The rate of slip is 0.12 ft/s.**

questions.question: Compounds with exactly two double carbon–carbon bonds are known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dienes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A molecule called diene **has** two double bonds between its carbon** atoms and is **unsaturated.**
 
• **Diene** is employed in industry as a** complex polymer's monomer constituent.** 
 
• It is also used in **Organic Synthesis.**
 
• Dienes are divided into** three groups** based on where the** double bond is located **relative to the rest of the molecule:
 
 
• A **cumulated diene** is one that has **two consecutive double bonds** on nearby Carbon atoms. They go by the name** Allene too.**
 
• A **conjugated diene** is a compound with **two conjugated double bonds** that are spaced apart by just** one bond.**
 
• **Two double bonds** that are spaced apart by** two or more double bond**s make up an** isolated diene.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terpenes:**

 
 
• Terpenes are a group of **organic compounds** with the formula** (C₅H₈)n,** where **n is greater than 1. **
 
 
 
• **Alkyne:**
 
 
• Alkynes are hydrocarbons that have **triple bonds between carbon atoms.**
 
• When it comes to** molecules with one triple bond**, their usual formula is **CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (and no rings).**
